newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cargill won't say if N.Korea agreed to food barter.
newsitem.headline: Cargill won't say if N.Korea agreed to food barter.

text.p: U.S. grain giant Cargill Inc held talks with North Korea last week on food barter trade, a Cargill Japan spokesman said on Monday, but he refused to disclose whether any deals were reached.
A delegation headed by Cargill Japan's president, Norwell Coquillard, arrived in Pyongyang last week for talks, the spokesman said.
"As a matter of policy, we can't disclose whether any deals were reached or not," he said.
Coquillard could not be reached for comment.
Earlier this month, the U.S. government granted Cargill permission to supply up to two million tonnes of grain to North Korea through barter trade.
Reclusive North Korea is gripped by near-famine conditions after two consecutive years of flooding, Korea experts say.
